Scope re-check (claude/peter):

- **Staleness policy: already done by A6b.** `Slot::take` ages a source out by `last_good` (not a failure count), so a hung or failing battery goes `Down` → `stand_down` idles the fleet. `World` serving the last reading forever is no longer possible on the live path.
- **Same-round gating: already done.** `run.rs` decides only on `(Fleet::Complete, Fresh)`. That's a run-loop property, not part of the fold.
- **What's left:**
  1. `Event::Meter.at` is the *tick* clock. The meter's own sample clock (`Delivery::Fresh(clock, _)`) gets dropped at `run.rs` `Fresh(_, sample)`. `DeviceUpdate.at` *is* the sample clock. So the journal can't tell when the meter was read, and meter/battery skew within a round (up to `request_timeout`, 2 s at a 3 s period) can't be recovered.
  2. `World` doesn't record when any reading was taken, so neither the controller nor analysis can see that skew. Epic A says the skew is what decides stability.
- `replay --verify` compares decision strings only, so new fields with `#[serde(default)]` keep old journal rows and `journey.json` readable. Changing `Meter.at` itself would move cooldown timing: a behaviour change that must not land before XJAYS3D's baseline.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `8bedaa1` on `fix/scan/failsafe-timing` (not pushed). `stand_down` writes to devices found `Down` on the outage's **first** failsafe tick only (`step.status.is_some()`), and filters them out after that.

Fork from the agent's first version, which skipped `Down` devices on every tick. I rejected that. `Down` means the reads stopped, and a parse failure or (after B1) an HTTP error status marks a slot `Down` while the box may still accept writes. That box would run its last command for the whole outage. One attempt per outage keeps the idle guarantee and costs at most one timed-out POST per outage, instead of one per tick. A device that goes down later in an outage was already idled by the ticks it answered on.

add.issue.name: Epic C: Dashboard v2

edit.description.md:
Implement the Dashboard v2 design handoff (claude.ai/design project a575f9d6…, `design_handoff_dashboard_v2/README.md` + `Home Energy.dc.html`). Four changes to the existing dashboard: SOC limits on the battery bar, pack list header + limit ticks, a new energy-flows chart, and a detail modal per entity.

Rebuild as Maud + Grass per CLAUDE.md *Dashboard styling*; htmx + native `<dialog>` + one light-DOM custom element (`assets/js/energy-flows.js`), no npm/bundler/Shadow DOM.

## Decisions (grilled 2026-10-08)
- **Min SOC tick = binding floor** `max(device minSoc, [tuning] min_soc)`; usable-energy math uses the same value.
- **Per-pack history** is rebuilt by re-parsing journalled `zendure_poll` raw captures — no journal schema change.
- **Car detail modal dropped** for v1: car SOC isn't journalled; the EV card stays non-clickable. EV is also out of the flows chart (no charge-power source).
- **Day navigation** is a follow-up ticket after today-only flows.
- **SSE dedupe** ships as its own ticket before the flows chart.
- **Mobile overflow** (860px / 375px, `scrollWidth <= innerWidth`) is checked manually and noted in each UI ticket's `Solution:`. There is no browser harness.
- **IntervalHistory ring = 100 buckets** (not 96): covers a 25 h DST day; "today since midnight" is otherwise always inside the rolling 24 h.
- Each ticket adds the tokens it consumes to `tokens.scss` (no unused tokens up front), and updates README where behavior changes.

add.issue.name: C1: SocLimits on DashboardState

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). Backend for the limit ticks.

- Add `SocLimits { min: Soc, max: Soc, balance_day: bool }` to `DashboardState`.
- `min` = binding floor `max(device minSoc, [tuning] min_soc)`. Device value comes from `DeviceTelemetry::min_soc` (already tracked in `run.rs` PollTelemetry). Use the same floor for the usable-energy calc so "of X kWh" agrees with the bar.
- `max` = `Controller::effective_max_soc(weekday)` (currently private, so expose it or lift it to a pure fn), with `balance_day` set on the balance weekday.
- Expose `usable_max = capacity × (max − min)` for the view.

Tests: binding floor picks the higher value; balance day yields 100% + flag.

add.issue.name: C4: SSE per-connection fragment dedupe

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). Prerequisite for C7 (the flows payload is ~500 rects and only changes when a bucket closes).

In `sse::fragment_stream`, keep the last payload sent per fragment for each connection, and skip the event when it is unchanged. This applies to every fragment.

Test: a payload equal to the last one sent is not emitted; a changed one is.

add.issue.name: C5: IntervalHistory — 15-min ring of flows and SOC

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). Data for the flows chart (C7) and detail modal (C10/C11).

- Extended by `meter_tick` and battery `DeviceUpdate`s. A single `record(&Event)` path is used for live, seed and (later) past days.

add.issue.name: C8: energy-flows.js custom element (interval, legend, readout, touch)

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). Depends on C7.

add.issue.name: C9: Energy flows day navigation (past days from the journal)

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). Depends on C7 + C8. A follow-up by decision; today-only ships first.

- `GET /fragments/energy-flows?day=YYYY-MM-DD&interval=1h|15m`. Parse `day` at the boundary into a local date (CONTROL-1): a future date clamps to today, an unparsable one returns 400.

add.issue.name: C14: Forecast axis tick labels overflow the panel on mobile

edit.description.md:

**Design decision (from the brief):** a fixed readout that updates in place, plus a crosshair. **No floating tooltips** anywhere: they cover the bars on a 180–260px chart and have nowhere to go at 375px. Hover never changes the modal's mini stats, which are 24 h aggregates.

**Markup (`line_chart`):**
- `div.line-chart__readout aria-live="polite"` in the chart head: `__readout-time` ("now" | "13:15–13:30", mono xs muted) and `__readout-value` ("+1.42 kW" | "63.0%", mono sm semibold).

- `line.line-chart__crosshair` (`--color-crosshair`, non-scaling stroke) and `div.line-chart__dot` (`--size-chart-dot` 9px, series color, 2px `--color-surface-raised` ring, `left/top` %).
- The default state is the latest bucket labelled "now", server-rendered; the readout is never empty. A gap bucket reads "—" and hides the dot.
- `view.rs` formats the values with the mini-stat formatter (`SignStyle::Explicit`, kW 2dp, % 1dp). **The JS only copies strings.**

**`assets/js/line-chart.js`** (~40 lines, light DOM):
- `pointermove` on the svg snaps to `round(offsetX / width × (n−1))` and updates the readout, crosshair and dot.
- Synced crosshairs: dispatch a bubbling `line-chart:hover {index}`. Every `line-chart` in the same `.modal__body` applies it, so the battery SOC and power charts move together.
- Mouse `pointerleave` sends `index: null`, which resets to "now". Touch: `pointerdown` pins and a tap outside unpins; use `touch-action: pan-y`.
- Optional: `tabindex="0"` with ← / → stepping one bucket and Home / End jumping to the ends.
- Modal content isn't SSE-swapped, so direct listeners are fine here (unlike energy-flows).

Tokens: `--size-chart-dot`, `--color-crosshair`.

**Out of scope (per brief):** forecast panel hover (no change this pass) and stat-card sparkline hover (the card is the modal's click target).

Tests: `data-values` / `data-times` / `data-y` have equal length; a gap bucket renders "—". Manual: battery SOC and power crosshairs move together; tap-pin on a phone; the readout falls back to "now".

Solution: 4e6088d on main. `state.rs` adds `IntervalIndex` (15-min intervals counted from the unix epoch, so DST can't repeat or skip one), plus `IntervalAverages`, `IntervalSlot` and `IntervalHistory` (100 buckets). A typed running mean keeps each average its own role type (Solar/Watts/Grid/BatteryPower), and each bucket also holds the last SOC. Home power is derived through the history's own `World`, the same way the stat card does it.

API:
- `record(&Event)`: a pure fold; `MqttTimeout` is ignored.
- `averages(idx)`
- `last_24h(now)`: 96 slots.
- `completed_on(date, tz, now)`: 100 slots on a 25 h day.
- `web::seed_interval_history(path, now)`: falls back to empty on a read error.
- `view.rs::hourly(&[IntervalSlot])` averages 4 quarters; its input must start on the hour (true for `completed_on`).
- `clock::local_day_start(date, tz)`.
- The read accessors carry `cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))` until C7 uses them.

- The seed window is the ring's full 25 h rather than 24 h, so "today" survives a restart late on a 25 h day.
- The startup device update may or may not be in the seed (async journal writer); the next poll fills it in.

add.issue.name: C16: IntervalHistory counts batteries that are no longer configured

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). From the wave-1 ultrareview of `6f6cf59..4e6088d` (main). **Reachable, medium.**

`IntervalHistory` keeps its own `World`, and `World.devices` is never pruned (`world.rs:152`). `battery_flow()` sums every device it has ever seen (`world.rs:181`). The startup seed folds every `device_update` from the last 25 h of journal. So after a battery swap or serial change, or a simulator run on the same journal path, the old device's last `current_power` is added to battery flow, and therefore to home usage, in every bucket. A restart doesn't clear it while those rows are still inside the window. `battery()` (lowest id) can also take SOC from the phantom device. The stat cards (live engine World) and the flows data then disagree.

**Fix:** `IntervalHistory` is built with the set of configured device ids, and `record` ignores a `DeviceUpdate` from any other id (live, seed and, later, C9 past days). Add a test with a journal that contains a foreign device id.

add.issue.name: C17: Wave-1 structure cleanup before wave 2 builds on it

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). From the wave-1 ultrareview of `6f6cf59..4e6088d` (main). The findings are cosmetic, but they land before C2/C6/C7/C10 build on these files.

- **Split files.** Move `Mean`, `Averaged`, `IntervalIndex`, `IntervalHistory` and their buckets out of `web/state.rs` (+80% this wave) into `web/intervals.rs`. Move the axis view types (`AxisPosition`/`AxisTick`/`AxisDensity`/`day_axis`) out of `view.rs` into `web/axis.rs` beside the component.
- **Coordinator stays thin** (run.rs is past 1k lines):
  - `state.intervals.record(&event)` moves inside `meter_tick`/`poll_tick`.
  - `SocLimits` is computed where the devices are folded and passed in, which deletes the `limits()` wrapper and `record_and_publish`'s new `engine`/`weekday` params.
  - The limits also refresh on meter ticks, so `balance_day` no longer lags midnight or goes stale during a device outage.
- **`usable_max` vs `usable`.** `usable_kwh` applies RTE but `usable_max` doesn't, so "X of Y kWh" would show 0.85·Y at a full bar. Apply the same RTE to both, and move `usable_max` to the web layer. `SocLimits` stays as the controller's SOC window.
- **`hourly` alignment comes from the type.** Group by `index.div_euclid(INTERVALS_PER_HOUR)` rather than a "must start on the hour" comment, so `hourly(&last_24h(now))` is correct.
- **RUST-2.**

add.issue.name: C19: A far-future timestamp blinds the interval ring until restart

edit.description.md:
Epic C (9PD6ETM). From the wave-1 ultrareview of `6f6cf59..4e6088d` (main). Low; reachable but rare.

The ring's `latest` index only moves forward. If the wall clock steps more than 25 h ahead and is then corrected (a bad NTP step), every later event fails the `within` window check and the flows chart stays empty until a restart. **Fix:** treat an event far behind `latest` that is plausibly "now" (e.g. within a few minutes of the event's own `sampled_at` vs `at`) as a clock correction and reset the ring, while still rejecting genuinely late journal rows (keep `a_late_event_from_before_the_ring_cannot_clobber_its_slot`).

This existed before C13 but sits squarely in its mobile scope. **Fix:** `minmax(0, 1fr)` columns, a narrower card padding and/or a smaller value size token at ≤860px. Also add `white-space: nowrap` on `pack-list__serial` so its ellipsis works.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: 3804652 on main.
- **Buckets:** each one holds per-pack figures keyed `PackKey { device, pack: PackId::{Serial | Position} }`: `PackInterval { soc: Extent<Soc>, temp: Extent<DeciKelvin>, charged, discharged: WattHours }`. Energy is the trapezoid between consecutive pack power readings, with no energy across a gap over 15 min or a backwards clock step (typed `Duration`s). The code is in the new `web/pack_intervals.rs`.
- **Live path:** `DashboardState::poll_tick` takes `polled_packs: Option<&[PackStatus]>`, i.e. this poll's own packs, not the remembered set.
- **Seed path:** `journal::read::read_raw_in_range` reads `zendure_poll` captures, and `zendure::packs_in_capture` re-parses them through the same `complete_packs` step as a live poll. There is no schema change. The live adapter only changed a literal to `POLL_CAPTURE`. An unparsable capture or one without `sn` is skipped; a foreign device is ignored (C16 filter).
- **For C12:** `IntervalHistory::packs_last_24h(now) -> BTreeMap<PackKey, Vec<PackSlot>>` (aligned with `last_24h`) and `PackInterval::combined(iter)` for 24 h totals.

Known difference: a capture is stamped at journal write, a few ms after the sample time, so seeded energy can differ very slightly from live. 622 + 6 tests pass.
